An API key can't be used to manage your account, sessions or API keys.

request.description: Links the provider account of an ID token to the signed-in user: get a nonce from `POST /v1/auth/{provider}/nonce`, put it in the SDK's (or Google Identity Services' or Sign in with Apple JS's) request, then send the ID token here. Send the password unless this session verified a second factor in the last 10 minutes. Signing in with a provider links an existing account by itself only when the provider manages the address (Gmail, Google Workspace, iCloud, Apple relay); otherwise sign-in answers `social_link_required` and the user links here. 201 with the identity; 200 when it was already linked.

request.description: Send the password unless this session verified a second factor in the last 10 minutes. Not allowed for the account's last way to sign in.

Starts a session (200). Browsers get an HttpOnly `__Host-session` cookie; native apps pass `"transport": "bearer"` and get the token in the response. For an account with two-factor authentication the response is 202 with `mfa.challenge_token` instead: finish with `POST /v1/auth/login/mfa`.

item.name: Finish signing in with a second factor

request.description: After a 202 from `POST /v1/auth/login`: send the challenge token with a code from the authenticator app, a recovery code, or a passkey's response (start it with `POST /v1/auth/login/mfa/passkey`). Each sign-in allows 5 attempts within 5 minutes; each code works once.
After a 202 from `POST /v1/auth/login` listing `passkey`: returns options limited to the account's passkeys. Send the response to `POST /v1/auth/login/mfa`.
Requires the password, and with two-factor authentication on a code, recovery code or passkey response (start one with `POST /v1/auth/passkeys/verification`). Signs out every device.
Send a code from the authenticator app or a passkey's response (start one with `POST /v1/auth/passkeys/verification`). Returns 10 new codes, shown once; the old codes stop working.

item.name: Set a new password with a reset code

request.description: Signs out every device. Two-factor authentication stays on, except on an account whose address wasn't verified yet: the code verifies it, as `POST /v1/auth/verify-email` does. Codes share the limit of `auth.code_attempts` a day per address (429).

Emails a 6-digit verification code. The response, and how long it takes, are the same whether or not the address already has an account. Registering again before verifying keeps the password only when it is the same; otherwise the account is left without one, and the owner sets it with `POST /v1/auth/password/forgot` after verifying.

item.name: Verify an email address with its code

request.description: Each code allows 5 attempts, and each address `auth.code_attempts` a day across codes (429). Verifying signs out every device and removes any passkey, authenticator app or Google, Apple or GitHub link added before the address was proven.
At most once a minute per address.

GitHub has no ID token for `POST /v1/auth/identities`, so a signed-in user links it through GitHub's page. Call this with the browser's credentials (fetch with `credentials: "include"`); it sets a short-lived cookie in that browser and returns the GitHub URL to open in it. Send the password unless this session verified a second factor in the last 10 minutes. GitHub returns to the callback, which links the GitHub account to this user, only while this session is active, and redirects to `return_to`, or to `return_to#error=<code>` (`identity_in_use`, `unauthenticated`, `invalid_state`, `access_denied`). Nobody is signed in by it.

item.name: Get a nonce for a native sign-in

request.description: Put the nonce in Google's or Apple's SDK request, then send the ID token with it to `POST /v1/auth/{provider}/token`. It works once, for 5 minutes.

item.name: Sign in with Google, Apple or GitHub in a browser

request.description: Open it in the browser (a link or redirect, not fetch): it sets a short-lived cookie and redirects to the provider. The provider returns to the callback, which redirects to `return_to` signed in, or with `#mfa_challenge_token=…&methods=…` for a second factor, or `#error=<code>`.
